newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-KINGS FIRE HEAD COACH GARRY ST. JEAN.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-KINGS FIRE HEAD COACH GARRY ST. JEAN.

text.p: Garry St. Jean, who coached the Sacramento Kings to their first playoff berth in 10 years but never finished above .500 in four-plus seasons, was fired Thursday.

Eddie Jordan, hired by St. Jean as an assistant five years ago, will take over the 28-39 team for the reaminder of the season. Assistant vice president of basketball operations Wayne Cooper will join assistants Mike Bratz and Pete Carril on the bench.

"Making a coaching change is never an easy decision, especially when you're dealing with a quality person like Garry St. Jean," Kings vice president of basketball operations Geoff Petrie said in a statement.
"This is a special opportunity for Eddie," said Petrie. "He has an excellent rapport with the players and he'll work hard to be successful."
It was the seventh NBA coaching change this season. St. Jean had the fifth-longest tenure of current NBA coaches.
A 105-100 victory over Denver on March 5 boosted Sacramento's record to 28-32, but the Kings are now in a seven-game losing streak.

The 42-year-old Jordan's NBA head coaching debut will be Friday at home against the lowly San Antonio Spurs. He had a six-year NBA career as a player and spent seven years as an assistant coach at the college level before joining the Kings.
"Garry St. Jean gave me my start with this team," Jordan said. "I've learned a lot from Saint. His philosophy was sound and his methods were effective.
"I'm very excited about this opportunity," he added. "I will work extremely hard to be effective and productive."

Despite the bad record, Sacramento was in the eighth and final playoff spot in the Western Conference, a half-game ahead of the Phoenix Suns with one more win in one more game. The Kings were two games behind the Los Angeles Clippers for seventh place.

"We had a window of opportunity to improve our playoff position, and that didn't happen," Petrie said. "I'm not standing up here putting all the blame on Garry. That would not be fair, but we felt we needed to do something to make a change."
The Kings have been hurt by injuries to forward Brian Grant and swingman Billy Owens.

St. Jean took over the Kings in 1992 and posted a 25-57 mark. The Kings improved by three wins the following season and registered back-to-back 39-43 campaigns, reaching the playoffs last season for the first time since 1986, their first season in Sacramento.
In his four-plus seasons with the Kings, St. Jean had a 159-236 (.403) record. He was an assistant under Don Nelson with the Golden State Warriors before joining the Kings.
Before the dismissal, St. Jean trailed only Utah's Jerry Sloan, Chicago's Phil Jackson, Houston's Rudy Tomjanovich and Seattle's George Karl in NBA tenure.
